FindNext/ReplaceRegex matched ^/$/\b against the search *range* boundaries, not real line start/end, causing false matches mid-line; fixed by padding the regex with a required leading/trailing '.' Issue #3571 (open, long-running since 2024-12): pasting on Windows Terminal causes cascading auto-indent ('staircase' effect) because Windows Terminal intercepts Ctrl-v itself and forwards pasted text to micro as individual key events rather than as a bracketed paste (EventPaste), so autoindent applies per character as if typed. Root cause (confirmed 2026-01 by JoeKar via raw-input tracing and comparing against Microsoft's edit and Windows Terminal source) is that micro/tcell's legacy Windows console backend never requests ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, so Windows Terminal never emits bracketed-paste sequences to it. Workarounds in the thread: rebind Paste to a non-intercepted key (e.g. Alt-v), or wrap Ctrl-v as 'setlocal autoindent off,Paste,setlocal autoindent on'. Confirmed fixed 2026-06/07 on the tcell/v3 branch, which does negotiate bracketed paste on Windows (verified working by both JoeKar and the reporter, with a noted redraw glitch on paste-over-selection and a status-bar PASTE indicator side effect).

new truecolor option (auto/on/off) replaces MICRO_TRUECOLOR env var; key finding: tcell already autodetects truecolor by default and micro was deliberately overriding it off, so the PR mostly exposes existing tcell behavior rather than adding new capability; default kept off initially for compat, later changed to auto (breaking change accepted after ~2 years of discussion); colorscheme tc/16-suffix naming inconsistencies noted as a follow-on problem

fixes #4050: concurrent sudo dd processes (truncate+write) raced on TCGETS2/TCSETS2, breaking sudo-rs; dmaluka traces the truncate-via-separate-dd design back to PR #3814/#3807 (need backup before truncate for safe sudo writes) and the eventual fix reorders safeWrite() to backup before openFile() for the sudo path (JoeKar's patch, adopted), returning OverwriteError on open failure; separately, the custom TTY pristine-state capture/restore around TempStart() overlaps tcell's own Init()/Fini() capture -- dmaluka suggests backporting tcell's Suspend()/Resume() instead but this PR keeps the local capture/restore; maintainers require commits split/squashed per their history preference; merged 2026-04-02 with a follow-up LookPath(sucmd) check to avoid spurious backups when sudo itself is missing

Issue #4041 (open): pushback against PR #3618's removal of plugin settings.json writes, from a user whose plugins (chromakeys, miscutils) relied on SetGlobalOption persisting. Long, heated debate over whether write-protection should be unconditional or configurable, whether micro's JSON5 support is 'real' if writes discard comments/formatting, and alternatives (separate plugin-owned config files, an in-place JSON patcher, a SetGlobalOptionAndSave action, a whitelist of trusted plugins). Maintainers (dmaluka, JoeKar, Neko-Box-Coder) converge on a single extensible string-valued option `writesettings` (comma-separated keywords, e.g. `set`, `plugins`) controlling which write paths (the `set`/`bind` commands vs. plugin calls) persist to settings.json/bindings.json, defaulting to `set` only (today's post-#3618 behavior: plugins never write) — rejecting a per-plugin whitelist and a combined set+plugins boolean as over-engineering. Landed via #4046 and #4055 (both close this issue).

new CursorToView{Top,Center,Bottom} actions to reposition cursor within the current view without scrolling; design settled through iteration: must account for soft-wrapped lines (SLoc not just line number) when checking if cursor is in view, scrollmargin is suppressed at buffer start/end to avoid unexpected jumps (deliberate, not a bug), multicursor state must be cleared via Buf.ClearCursors() before the move (RemoveAllMultiCursors() reorders badly since it itself calls Relocate()); explicitly NOT meant to fix PageUp/PageDown's cursor-jumps-to-top behavior — that's deferred to a separate action/behavior-change discussion (nano-style paging, referencing #1808) so as not to break existing user expectations by changing CursorPageUp/Down semantics directly

PR generalizes save-before-close prompt (open/term/quit) into closePrompt, and adds Buffer.Shared() to skip the prompt when another buffer already has the file open (matches #3559 for quit); review exposed that onSave/onSaveAs/preSave firing rules are undocumented and inconsistent across Save/SaveAs/quit-prompt paths (also seen in #3550, #3689) — maintainers decided documenting the mess is more realistic than unifying it

comment.lua commenttype override was clobbered on filetype change; fix (JoeKar) introduces comment.type via RegisterCommonOption plus DoSetOptionNative -- the key distinction dmaluka documents is that SetOptionNative marks an option as locally-overridden (survives reload/filetype change) while DoSetOptionNative just sets the buffer value without that mark, so per-filetype computed defaults must use DoSetOptionNative or they freeze at first value; commenttype renamed to comment.type with backward-compat alias kept permanently (dmaluka: no noisy runtime warning, just a doc note it may be deprecated later); recurring maintainer ask for one-functional-change-per-commit history for bisectability

PR #2810 (merged): fixes 13 separate syntax-highlighting bugs (bash, PHP, JS, Ruby, C/C++, etc.) whose root cause was the highlighter incorrectly gating regex matches containing literal ^ or $ characters behind a canMatchStart/canMatchEnd flag pair meant to represent line-start/line-end anchors -- but Go regexp/RE2 treats ^ and $ inside a pattern as matching every line-tokenized chunk passed to it (not just the true first/last line), so the gating silently dropped valid rule matches on later lines. JoeKar traced this via debug logging and screenshot comparisons against Vim/Emacs/Neovim, and the fix removes the start/end tracking entirely rather than trying to special-case it. zyedidia (owner) accepted the tradeoff of "compromising some incremental highlight performance" since most files are not huge, and noted the syntax highlighting system needs a full rework (linking the stalled github.com/zyedidia/flare project) that only lacked time/language files -- a separate, earlier rework attempt than the one tracked in [[highlighter-performance]].

Merged PR splitting InitLocalSettings into UpdatePathGlobLocals (path globs, checked on every reload) and UpdateFileTypeLocals (ft: block, checked only when filetype resolves) so ReloadSettings(true) fires onBufferOptionChanged/OptionCallback when filetype actually changes; review caught a glob-locals regression (only worked after `> reload`), a crash from `ft:` settings.json entries, and settled that filetype changes need SetOptionNative-style callback firing via a new doCallbacks helper shared by DoSetOptionNative.

Closed issue: bindings.json can't bind raw terminal escape sequences like \x1bOC/\x1bOD (e.g. MobaXterm's CtrlShiftLeft/Right) because JSON string literals reject arbitrary \xHH escapes, producing "invalid character 'x' in string escape code"; duplicate of the same limitation reported earlier in #1863. JoeKar (maintainer) began checking whether bindings.go's handling of a 0x1b-prefixed sequence (per keybindings.md's own description of terminal escape events) is sufficient to support such bindings some other way.

Merged docs PR rewriting runtime/help/plugins.md; maintainer dmaluka's review establishes that plugin help docs must stay readable as plain text inside micro, not just as rendered markdown, and pushed back on a footnote-style link reference for being confusing under that constraint; he also corrected a claim that plugins are merely unlikely to load syntax header files, noting RTSyntaxHeader is not exported to Lua so they cannot do so at all, and asked for consistent indentation on function-description continuation lines.

Merged PR making PluginRepository.Fetch/PluginChannel.Fetch report skipped plugin repos informatively instead of dumping raw JSON-decode errors; settled on using stdlib http.StatusText(resp.StatusCode) for all non-200 statuses (dmaluka) rather than hand-rolled per-code messages, and on returning nil instead of PluginPackages{} everywhere for consistency (JoeKar); related to the still-open #3389 which additionally wants a fetch timeout so a slow/unstable repo host doesn't block other plugins.

Merged PR renames Plugin.Default to Builtin (JoeKar: "Builtin is somehow more self explaining... wouldn't require the additional comment") and changes `-plugin list` to print "(built-in)" instead of a version for bundled plugins, since their bundled version never gets updated and so is useless, while still showing a real version if the user's own ~/.config/micro/plug copy overrides a built-in one and its Builtin flag isn't set; initlua is deliberately excluded from Builtin (dmaluka: "it doesn't come with micro, it is created by the user") and printed bare with no version/suffix at all; a parenthesization bug (`|| p.Name == "initlua"` sitting outside the enclosing condition) made every successful `-plugin remove` print "Default plugins cannot be removed" even though removal still succeeded via `continue`, fixed alongside renaming the message to name the specific built-in plugin.

Merged PR fixing leaked file handles on Windows (unclosed files blocked git branch switches) by adding missing file.Close() calls in safeWrite()/ReOpen() error paths, and refactoring the backup step into a new writeBackup() helper; review (dmaluka, JoeKar) reaffirmed the deliberate ordering from #3273 that forceKeepBackup must stay false until the backup write actually succeeds, so a failed write/close leaves the backup around for retry rather than silently discarding it, and flagged that the new code path still leaves forceKeepBackup=true if safeWrite's file.Close() itself errors.

Merged PR adding/refining the nftables.yaml syntax-highlighting file; the whole thread is routine line-by-line regex/style nitpicking specific to that one filetype (operator grouping, hex-vs-decimal number matching, indentation consistency, filename-detection regex) with no generalizable rule about micro's syntax-highlighting mechanism itself, just cleanup of a stalled contributor's syntax file before merge.

Merged core fix: micro's tab layout is a tree of Type/Type Node children (visualized via bp:Tab():String()), and quitting a nested pane inside e.g. HSplit->VSplit->HSplit can leave a "chained parent" — a node with a single child left over from the unsplit — that isn't collapsed, so a later resize call hits the wrong parent and proportional resize degrades (e.g. 50/25/25 instead of an even 33/33/33 across three HSplits); the fix simplifies/collapses the tree on unsplit so chained single-child parents don't survive to confuse later resize calculations.

Long-running closed issue: Shift+Up/Down often fail to extend selection (while Shift+Left/Right work) because many terminals/multiplexers (tmux, xfce4-terminal, Konsole, macOS Terminal.app) either don't send an escape sequence for those combos or intercept them as their own shortcuts (tab switching, line scroll); zyedidia's own workaround (cross-referenced from #983) is a bindings.json override using explicit CSI-sequence entries written as JSON unicode escapes (safe, unlike the raw hex escapes that broke #2950) for Select*/Move*/Word* actions, and setting TERM=xterm-256color helps in some tmux setups but not others; root cause was never tracked down by the maintainer.

Long-running open issue on Ctrl-C not copying: maintainer dmaluka rules "this is not a bug in micro, this is a terminal emulator issue" — a terminal either consumes Ctrl-C itself (as its own copy-to-clipboard shortcut) or passes it through to the running application, never both, so when the terminal consumes it micro never receives the byte at all (diagnosable by running micro's `raw` command and checking whether pressing Ctrl-C prints anything); he doubts any terminal implements a mode-aware split (consume in command-line mode, pass through in full-screen/application mode) though kitty's `send_text application` looked promising and didn't pan out when tried; separately, several commenters report `set clipboard terminal`/`set clipboard external` (the latter needing xclip/wl-copy installed) as the fix for their case, so the terminal-consumes-the-shortcut explanation is not the only cause in this thread.

Open issue tracking the long-standing lack of built-in .conf/.cfg syntax highlighting: neitsab found micro used to highlight conf files until commit 975e78d9c0 deliberately removed the conf syntax definition (too many conflicts with other filetypes' detection); current workarounds are a user-authored ~/.config/micro/syntax/conf.yaml, or mapping "*.conf" to filetype "ini" via settings.json, or (per Andriamanitra) the default.yaml fallback mechanism added in #2933, which ships with no ini/conf rules out of the box so users must supply their own default.yaml; six other issues (#2466, #3401, #3751, #4004, #4021) are cross-referenced duplicates of the same request.

Man-page/-help rewrite surfaced (dmaluka, in review) micro's actual CLI cursor-position semantics: `FILE:LINE[:COL]` only takes effect if the `parsecursor` option is enabled, while `+LINE[:COL]` always works regardless of that option but is a single argument applied to every file opened on the command line rather than per-file; the two forms are mutually exclusive and `+LINE[:COL]` takes priority, so `micro foo:10 bar +20` opens both `foo` and `bar` at line 20, not `foo` at 10; if several `+LINE[:COL]` args are given only the last is applied; and `+LINE[:COL]` is still honored even with no file argument, opening an unnamed empty buffer with the cursor at that (nonexistent) line/column.

Merged PR fixing a real race between the async highlighter goroutine and main-goroutine buffer edits (lines freed mid-highlight caused sporadic macOS CI failures/deadlocks); design settled through review (dmaluka): drop the abandoned per-line NoLock/Lock function-duplication approach in favor of a single whole-LineArray mutex plus keeping the existing per-line locks for state/match (so displayBuffer only waits on one line's lock, not the whole array), have HighlightStates/HighlightMatches/ReHighlightStates lock-check-unlock per iteration (`for i:=0;;i++ { input.Lock(); if i>=input.LinesNum(){Unlock();break}; ...; input.Unlock() }`) so the highlighter itself validates the current line count under lock rather than trusting a stale LinesNum() snapshot, and add explicit Buffer.Lock()/Unlock() around Retab's raw append into `b.lines[i].data` (noted as separately buggy - bypasses EventHandler so retab can't be undone - but deferred as a distinct issue); benchmarking showed no real throughput cost from the fix itself, the apparent 10x slowdown was from re-enabling InitRuntimeFiles(false) in the test, not the locking.

Long-closed issue diagnosed by owner zyedidia as a PuTTY bug, not a micro bug: PuTTY sends the wrong escape codes for Shift/Ctrl+arrow key combinations, breaking keyboard-driven selection (mouse selection is unaffected and works fine) — verified by comparing against KiTTY, a PuTTY fork that sends the correct codes and was recommended as a workaround at the time; a 2024 comment gives an actual PuTTY-side fix that avoids needing KiTTY: in PuTTY 0.79, under Terminal -> Keyboard, set "Shift/Ctrl/Alt with the arrow keys" to "xterm-style bitmap".

Closed issue collecting the community's workarounds for a transparent (terminal-matching) background, since micro has no dedicated transparency option: omitting the background half of `color-link default "[fg],[bg]"` in a custom colorscheme falls back to the terminal's own background; any 16-color colorscheme (e.g. the built-in "simple") works because 16-color schemes don't hardcode an opaque bg; or explicitly set the bg to `#00000000` in a copied colorscheme file under ~/.config/micro/colorschemes for finer control.

Merged PR fixing SharedBuffer identity for the same file opened via different symlinks (so undo history etc is correctly shared) by adding util.ResolvePath(), replacing plain filepath.Abs() calls in NewBuffer/saveToFile; extensive review settled several subtleties: must resolve every path component (not just the final file) since any intermediate symlink or the CWD itself can be a symlink, must resolve relative-to-absolute at each iteration since an intermediate symlink target can itself be relative, and for a not-yet-existing file (new/unsaved) ResolvePath walks up via filepath.Dir/EvalSymlinks until it finds an existing ancestor then rejoins the non-existent remainder so dir/file and dir1/file (dir1 -> dir) still resolve to the same absolute path; separately settled that when two symlinks/paths reach the same file, the statusline keeps showing whichever name was opened first ("first wins", deliberately not resolved like vim first appeared to do), and that Buffer.Fini() should only Serialize()/CancelBackup() when closing the last (non-shared) instance of a buffer, since each serialize just overwrites the previous cursor-position record. TOCTOU on the resolved path was acknowledged but explicitly left unaddressed - micro doesn't hold a file handle across a buffer's lifetime.

Merged PR debugging why tools/build-version.go (git describe --tags-based version string, used by both make and CI) fell back to "0.0.0-unknown" in GitHub Actions: root cause was actions/checkout's default shallow clone giving `git describe --tags` nothing to find, fixed by adding `fetch-depth: 0` and `fetch-tags: true` to the checkout step in both nightly.yaml and test.yaml (superseding the old build-version.go-internal `git fetch --tags` fallback, which was also flagged as an unwanted side effect for a version-reporting tool to have, and which can fail outright in the upstream repo because the nightly workflow's own force-updated "nightly" tag causes `git fetch --tags` to reject as "would clobber existing tag"); also added `workflow_dispatch` to nightly.yaml so it can be tested on demand instead of waiting for the daily cron, and added stderr-printing `log.Printf` calls around each semver parse/exec fallback in build-version.go so future version-string failures are diagnosable instead of silent.

Closed PR proposing a built-in formatter plugin; the review thread renders to roughly 42KB, past what this pass could load in full, so this verdict rests only on the visible opening exchange — JoeKar questioning whether a separate enable option is needed at all since activating the plugin already implies the functionality — which is an unresolved single question, not a settled convention or maintainer ruling, so nothing citable was actually captured.

Multi-cursor support for the comment plugin: reworked toggleCommentSelection to operate over a table of lines gathered from all cursors rather than a single start/end range, with cursor positions restored via per-cursor displacement afterward; maintainer JoeKar also stated a position against a start-of-line/unindented comment placement option (issue #2282), preferring the current indented alignment as the default, and pushed for rebase-not-merge history hygiene on long-lived PRs.

Long discussion arriving at the final runtime/syntax/sh.yaml option-highlighting regex: settled on (\s|^)(-[A-Za-z0-9]+|--[A-Za-z0-9][\w-]*|--(\s|$)) after debating whether to match --a single-letter long opts (yes, getopt_long allows them, GNU truncation like --v for --version is real), whether to highlight bare -- (yes, marks end-of-options), the \s+ prefix missing line-continuation cases (foo \ \n --bar), and accepting --------- as a known false positive since Go regexp lacks lookahead/lookbehind for a cleaner fix.

Maintainer zyedidia explains the clipboard option: with clipboard=internal (the default), micro never touches the system clipboard, so ctrl-c/ctrl-v inside micro only round-trip through micro's own buffer while the terminal's own paste (e.g. cmd-v/right-click) still delivers the OS clipboard, producing the confusing symptom of ctrl-v pasting stale cut text instead of what was just copied; the fix on macOS is to set clipboard to external, and on WSL the system clipboard needs an xclip-shim workaround (e.g. Konfekt/xclip-xsel-WSL) since there's no X server.

Fixed a crash where BufMapEvent's chained-action loop kept calling execAction after the current pane changed to a non-BufPane (TermPane/InfoPane), by breaking when CurPane() returns nil; CurPane() stays typed *action.BufPane for Lua/plugin-API stability rather than becoming the generic Pane interface, since gopher-luar has no Go type-assertion support for plugins to narrow it back down. Maintainers noted two real remaining gaps this PR does not close: chained keybindings still silently stop rather than actually working once they hit a non-buf pane (#2307, #2288 crashes are fixed but the bindings still don't do what the user wanted), and onAction/preAction callbacks are still unsupported for non-buf panes (#2677). The success/innerSuccess return-value plumbing in bufAction was found to be unused except by InfoPane's DoKeyEvent, which is untangled separately in PR #3267.

Long-running issue distinguishing delete (no clipboard side-effect) from cut (Ctrl-K, which overwrites the system buffer): no built-in delete-only-line action exists, but the durable workaround given by the owner and reaffirmed by other users is rebinding a key to the chained action "SelectLine,Delete" in bindings.json, e.g. {"CtrlK": "SelectLine,Delete"}, which also avoids the noticeable clipboard-sync delay over SSH with X11 forwarding. Known residual gap: the Alt-g keybinding help screen still shows the stock "^K Cut line" label even after such a rebind, since it reflects the default action name rather than the user's override.

Added vim-style `+/REGEX` CLI arg support (e.g. `micro +/imem_size +623 file.c`) alongside the existing `+LINE[:COL]`, landing as a new internal/buffer.Command{StartCursor, SearchRegex, SearchAfterStart} struct that replaces the old NewBufferFromFileAtLoc/NewBufferFromStringAtLoc cursor-only API (now NewBufferFromFileWithCommand/NewBufferFromStringWithCommand) — deliberately generalized past just the CLI since dmaluka noted the same "command" concept applies to vim/vi/ed/sed-style runtime use later. SearchAfterStart (true when +/REGEX appears after +LINE:COL in argv) replaces an earlier CommandOrder enum with a plain bool. Regex safety was scoped explicitly: only constant regex fragments used internally are compiled with regexp.MustCompile, while the actual user-supplied search text reuses the existing (already-crash-prone per #3700, the `+/\Q` panic) FindNext search path rather than adding a new unguarded MustCompile on user input. A real bug caught in review: forgetting to update the cursor's OrigSelection alongside CurSelection when a `+/TEXT` match sets the initial selection, which broke Shift+Right/Shift+Down extension after opening with a search.

Fixes the #3700 crash where a search regex containing `\Q` without a closing `\E` (e.g. bare `\Q`) panicked instead of erroring, by making internal/buffer/search.go's findLineParams surface regexp.Compile errors instead of relying on regexp.MustCompile on padded patterns; error messages now reach the user (previously swallowed) via a related actions.go fix making `err != nil` and `found` mutually exclusive branches. Per Go maintainer confirmation (golang/go#76424) `\Q` without `\E` is actually valid regex syntax meaning "quote to end of string", so the fix auto-corrects it by re-compiling with a trailing `\E` appended and using that if it succeeds, rather than rejecting it as an error — this recovery only runs when padMode is nonzero (i.e. actually needed) to avoid extra compiles per line. The same regex validation was found to need consistent handling in the `replace` command path too (ReplaceRegex could still crash pre-fix); it turned out already covered because both search and replace funnel through findLineParams.

Merged PR (dmaluka) adds two options, both off by default: hltaberrors highlights tab/space indentation errors using the tabstospaces setting as the criterion (tab chars flagged when tabstospaces is on, leading spaces flagged when it's off), and hltrailingws highlights trailing whitespace but suppresses the highlight on the line currently being typed until the cursor leaves it, so normal in-progress typing isn't flagged, only whitespace left behind after moving on.

Rejected feature request to default to space indentation instead of tabs. Owner's rationale for keeping tabs as the default: the tab key should insert a literal tab character by default, and options exist for exactly this kind of preference (tabstospaces in settings.json) rather than changing defaults and forcing a config-upgrade disruption on existing users; a contributor separately noted Go source itself conventionally uses tabs. For users who want automatic per-file indent-style detection (not just a fixed default), the recommended combo is enabling tabtospaces plus the third-party dmaluka/micro-detectindent plugin, since micro has no built-in auto-detection.

Long-running community thread on copying/pasting over SSH: owner zyedidia explains micro on a remote host cannot reach the local machine's clipboard, so the terminal emulator must do the copy (its own modifier+select) rather than micro; xclip/xsel on the remote host make ctrl-c/ctrl-v reach a local X server via ssh -X but add a large per-operation delay (xsel worse than xclip) and X11 mouse-selection auto-fills PRIMARY on every selection, causing multi-second freezes, so several users end up uninstalling them; the eventual clean fix is setting "clipboard": "terminal" together with a terminal that supports OSC 52 (e.g. Alacritty), and absent that, ctrl+shift+c/ctrl+shift+v (terminal-owned) vs ctrl+c/ctrl+v (micro-owned) is the workaround split to know, since Shift+select routes through the terminal instead of micro.

Micro was published to Flathub as io.github.zyedidia.micro (accepted 2023-04) after several appdata/metainfo.xml fixes (PRs #2792, #2793, #2796, #2803, the last adding type="desktop-application" so it would actually appear in the store rather than just being installable). Practical flatpak-specific facts users hit afterward: config lives at ~/.var/app/io.github.zyedidia.micro/config/micro, not the native ~/.config/micro (both can exist simultaneously with different contents if the native binary was also run); flatpaks cannot install an executable onto $PATH, so running it as plain `micro` requires a shell alias/function wrapping `flatpak run io.github.zyedidia.micro`, and the same command string is what to put in $EDITOR. As of the last comment (2024-12) the flathub listing was still unverified (no response on verification request), and a separate "flathub package out of date" issue (#2980) exists as staleness follow-up.

Merged fix for the pane-split Node tree's root-node handling (fixes crash issue #3980): the root node was identified by Kind==STUndef, but that sentinel became stale after the first split (root's Kind gets set to STVert/STHoriz and never reset), so later unsplit/quit logic misbehaved; the agreed fix identifies the root structurally via node.parent==nil instead, with flatten() given a special case for the root (copies the sole remaining child's fields into place, keeping parent nil) and STUndef is reset only when the flattened root ends up with zero children (i.e. truly back to the single-pane initial state) rather than whenever it becomes root — getting this wrong caused two follow-up crashes (nil pointer dereference on unsplit, and wrong resize when the intermediate node being flattened away had multiple grandchildren); String() debug output prints "-"/"|" by Kind rather than a special "/" for root, since a root with children is otherwise structurally the same as any other split node.

Merged PR reworks CursorPageUp/Down (and SelectPageUp/Down) to behave nano/vim-like: instead of jumping a full view-height and losing place, they scroll by (view height - pageoverlap) while moving the cursor the same amount, keeping a fixed line-overlap between pages; adds the new "pageoverlap" setting (default 2, validated non-negative) rather than reusing scrollmargin, because maintainer dmaluka argued scrollmargin (used while slow-scrolling) and page overlap are conceptually different and a user may want one at zero while keeping the other. Multi-cursor correctness required guarding the view-scroll calls with h.Cursor.Num==0 so the view is scrolled only once per keypress, not once per cursor (the naive multi-cursor version scrolled the view far away since ScrollUp/Down and MoveCursorUp/Down were both called per-cursor via MultiActions). The remaining scrollmargin-during-paging interaction is intentional and kept via the existing h.Relocate() call: paging respects scrollmargin the same way normal cursor movement does, matching vim's scrolloff behavior, rather than adding a fancier direction-aware relocate.

Wide-ranging 2018 keybinding Q&A that pins down several durable facts about micro's terminal-dependent key handling: (1) Shift-Backspace is fundamentally indistinguishable from plain Backspace because most terminals send the identical escape sequence — inspect what a terminal actually sends with the `> raw` command; (2) Alt bindings are case-sensitive (Alt-g != Alt-G, the latter meaning Alt-Shift-g) while non-Alt letter bindings are not; (3) any key to enter command mode (default CtrlE) can be freely rebound by rebinding the `CommandMode` action in bindings.json, and likewise any command can be bound directly via the `command:<cmd>` prefix (puts it in the command bar and runs it) or `command-edit:<cmd>` (places it in the command bar for further editing without running) — these two prefixes were added directly in response to this issue; (4) command-mode text supports tab-completion of command names (type `vs`+Tab -> `vsplit`); (5) Mac Terminal.app and Alacritty are called out as poor for Alt/Shift+arrow combos because they emit Unicode chars instead of escape sequences for Alt, unlike iTerm2 (fixable there via Preferences->Profiles->Keys->Left option key->Esc+); (6) the xterm modifier-code convention micro follows: modifier digit 2=Shift, 3=Alt, 4=Shift+Alt, 5=Ctrl, 6=Shift+Ctrl, 7=Alt+Ctrl, 8=Shift+Alt+Ctrl, appended into sequences like `\x1b[1;<N>A/B/C/D` for arrows, vs plain `\x1b<char>` for Alt+letter — cited when helping alacritty maintainers add correct escape output. A `run <cmd>` command already existed for backgrounded shell commands distinct from interactive ShellMode (CtrlB); a request for an IDE-style persistent output pane went unimplemented in core (third-party attempt: sum01/cmdlog-micro, described as broken/pre-release).

Recurring "why doesn't Cmd-C/Cmd-V work like other Mac editors" confusion, explained by the owner as an architectural limit rather than a bug: micro is terminal-based and only receives key events the terminal application chooses to forward, and on Mac the terminal reserves Cmd-key combos for its own keybindings (e.g. Cmd-Q to close the terminal, Cmd-T new tab), so Cmd events generally never reach micro at all — there is no code path in micro that could special-case Cmd even if desired. Cmd-V often appears to "work" only because the terminal's own paste binding sends the clipboard contents as a stream of ordinary character key events, not because micro sees a real Cmd-V event; Cmd-C does not work to copy because micro's selection state is internal to micro and the terminal has no way to know what's selected. Users wanting Cmd-based bindings must remap at the terminal-app or OS level (e.g. BetterTouchTool) to emit the Ctrl/character sequences micro can actually receive.

Open draft PR (glupi-borna) implementing the overlay/popup-layer API following the design sketched in a comment on issue #3465: keeps the Go-side surface minimal, deliberately pushing composition complexity to the plugin side for flexibility, and ships two example plugins (a cursor-adjacent autocomplete overlay and a search/palette widget) plus a more involved quickmenu input-box example, all built around an immediate-mode style for handling overlay events since proper event handling in plugin code was found to be non-trivial to get right; author explicitly does not want the example plugins to become default, they exist only to demonstrate the API in this draft.

Recurring "copy doesn't reach my local clipboard over SSH" reports, with the owner's standing explanation: micro on the remote host has no access to the local clipboard at all, since it is the terminal (running locally) that owns the connection to the OS clipboard. Two real fixes exist, not one: (1) disable micro's own mouse handling (`set mouse off` or equivalently the `mouse` setting) so raw mouse selection is handled by the local terminal itself, which then owns Ctrl-Shift-C/Cmd-C copy — downside noted by a user: terminal-native selection can't scroll to grab text past the visible window, unlike micro's own selection; (2) set micro's `clipboard` option to `terminal` to use the OSC52 escape-sequence protocol, which lets micro ask the (OSC52-supporting) terminal to write to the local clipboard over the SSH connection without disabling micro's mouse support — documented in `> help copypaste`. A third, narrower workaround needs no config change at all: holding Shift while mouse-selecting (fn on Mac) bypasses the running application's mouse-reporting entirely for that one selection, letting the terminal's own copy shortcut (e.g. Ctrl-Shift-C in gnome-terminal) grab exactly what's visible on screen.

Owner zyedidia's fix for shift-arrow text selection (and ctrl/ctrl-shift-arrow) not working under the bare Linux console (TERM=linux): the console driver doesn't send those escape sequences at all, so it needed both a kmap remapping the relevant keycodes to custom escape sequences (a supplemental.kmap adapted from the tilde editor, loaded via loadkeys, one-time per boot not per login) and a matching change in micro itself to recognize those custom sequences under TERM=linux; setting TERM=xterm is a workaround that makes it work without the kmap but breaks other console apps that rely on TERM=linux behavior (e.g. mc's F3/F4), so it's not recommended. The instructions ended up documented on the project wiki.

Closed/superseded-by-#1762 PR that nonetheless carries the real design debate behind the `hlsearch` (highlight-all-search-matches) feature. Two architectures were weighed: (A) this PR's approach, extending pkg/highlight.Highlighter with a "custom pattern" overlay layer (AddCustomPattern/RemoveCustomPattern/highlightCustomMatches) reusing the syntax highlighter's match-storage machinery — rejected long-term because it couples custom highlighting to the syntax highlighter, making it harder to later swap in a different syntax engine (tree-sitter, #1466), and risks matches diverging from what FindNext finds; (B) the eventually-adopted #1762 approach, a LineArray-based per-line result cache computed via repeated FindNext calls. A naive "just search every visible line on every display call" alternative was measured and rejected: regex search is expensive enough (confirmed by CPU profiling) that doing it on every redraw made hlsearch the most battery-draining part of micro, which is why #1762 caches per-line results instead of recomputing them each frame. Also surfaced and fixed in this line of work: BufPane.HighlightCustomPattern lets Lua plugins highlight arbitrary regex patterns with colorscheme-group colors (independent feature, kept in the final implementation) and the default hlsearch style is an underline (owner's preference, for a "more subtle" look distinguishable from selection) rather than reversed colors, contrary to the author's own preference for a colored background — colorschemes can override via `color-link hlsearch "..."`.

Long-requested feature: soft-wrap at a fixed column (not the pane's right edge), useful for prose/writing workflows; existing workaround from dmaluka is a dummy left-hand vertical split resized (via ResizePane, mouse drag, or a small init.lua/plugin) so the working pane's width equals the desired wrap column, but this is fragile (percentage-based ResizePane needed because terminal startup geometry races with micro's own startup resize, and pre-#1800-fix versions call onBufPaneOpen before the pane is fully initialized) and the requester ultimately found the extra split more distracting than the long lines it fixed, preferring a real margin/column option over a workaround pane. The repo's own account (ddaanet) posted a concrete design settled and later implemented as issue #4142: a `softwrapcolumn` integer common option, default 0 (off, current behavior), wraps at that column when >0 and softwrap is on, clamped to pane width so a narrow pane still wraps at its edge, deliberately kept orthogonal to both `wordwrap` and `colorcolumn` (colorcolumn is a visual guide only and coupling it to wrapping would surprise people who set it for the ruler alone), with continuation rows still starting at column 0 so cursor/loc mapping is untouched.

Introduces internal/display/softwrap.go and the core softwrap data model still in use: SLoc{Line, Row} represents a vertical scroll position as a buffer line number plus a visual row (sub-line) within it, replacing plain int line numbers everywhere scrolling math is done (View.StartLine is now an SLoc). BufWindow.getRow(loc) computes which visual row a buffer.Loc falls in via width := w.Width - w.gutterOffset (minus scrollbar column) then util.StringWidth(...)/width — this is the concrete site where wrapping width is derived from live pane geometry rather than any setting, confirming there is no config knob to intercept here without patching this function. getRowCount(line) is getRow of the line's last character + 1, i.e. how many visual rows a given buffer line occupies when wrapped. Scroll(s, n)/Diff(s1, s2) do SLoc-aware arithmetic (scrollUp/scrollDown/diff helpers) so page-up/down, centering, and Relocate work correctly across wrapped lines; before this PR these operations used plain buffer-line arithmetic and broke under softwrap (issues #632, #1657). BufWindow.Bottomline() was removed as fundamentally broken under softwrap and replaced by `w.Scroll(v.StartLine, height-1)`. A noted still-open edge case: getRow's width-based row computation "doesn't work quite correctly if there is an incomplete tab or wide character at the end of a row" (#1979). Follow-on softwrap work (cursor up/down within a wrapped line, word wrapping) continued in PR #2076.

Long-standing Windows issue: micro exits immediately with "No suitable screen available" in some terminal setups (mintty/Cygwin/Babun, sometimes cmd/PowerShell). Root cause per community investigation: tcell (micro's terminal library) does not support termios on Windows and errors out in terminals like mintty that rely on it. Workarounds found: unset the TERM environment variable (a stray TERM=xterm or MICRO_TRUECOLOR=1 leftover triggers the failure on cmd/PowerShell) fixes it there but loses truecolor; for mintty specifically, running via `winpty micro` works except mouse input is then unsupported. No actual code fix landed in-thread; maintainer dmaluka later asked (2024) whether it's still reproduced on a recent version, unanswered as of the last update.

No built-in LSP support and zyedidia never committed to a timeline beyond a 2020 "maybe after keybinding rework" remark; the de facto solution is the community plugin AndCake/micro-plugin-lsp (hover/definition/references/format via alt-K/D/R/F), with known UX problems reported by users: forced/aggressive autocompletion that deletes trailing line content and can't be limited to an explicit trigger key, long hover text not fitting the screen, and backspace performance degradation while LSP is active; issue was closed "Won't Do" by the filing newcomer (not the owner) after 5 years, with later activity pointing to discussion #3231 instead.

Recurring request for a built-in tree-view file browser sidebar met sustained pushback from the community (not zyedidia, who never weighed in) on the grounds that micro's niche is between nano and a full IDE and a sidebar risks scope creep; the de facto resolution is community plugins doing it instead (filetree-plugin, filemanager-plugin, files-plugin), with reported friction being focus-stealing on toggle (worked around via an onViewOpen hook restoring CurView) and uncertainty over whether plugins can receive mouse input to click tree items; issue remains open with no core movement as of 2022.

Long-running PR (2024 to still-open draft in 2026) reworking the regex-based syntax highlighter after dmaluka diagnosed the real bug: highlighting time grows exponentially with the number of same-line nested/sibling regions (not merely slow rune decoding), which explains several reported hangs/CPU-pegging issues (closes #2839, #3115, #3487, #3765, #3776, #4018); the new region/pattern-storage algorithm fixes real correctness bugs too (XML self-closing tags, nested same-marker string regions) but repeated review rounds from dmaluka found the overlap-detection logic ad-hoc and hard to explain even by its own author, so JoeKar converted it back to draft in April 2025 pending a larger simplification; a separate architectural idea surfaced here but deliberately split out to #3149 is replacing micro's per-line byte-array storage with pre-decoded runes (or SciTE-style byte/rune index spans) to kill the repetitive utf8.DecodeRune cost on long lines; both JoeKar and dmaluka agree regex can never correctly parse arbitrary XML/HTML and that only an LSP-backed approach would be fully correct, but integrating LSP into highlighting is called out as a "longer road...never started nor finalized", so regex remains the fallback approach by design.

Years-long recurring bug (2017-2020, v1.3.x through v2.0.1) where mouse movement/scroll injected garbage text or control codes into the buffer, or froze the terminal; root cause per zyedidia was tcell reading an incomplete escape sequence (e.g. terminal splits \x1b[ from the following mouse-event payload across two reads), causing the prefix to be misinterpreted as a keybinding (like Alt-[) and the remainder inserted as literal text, fixed iteratively in zyedidia's tcell fork (first a naive 10ms read-delay hack, then proper partial-sequence state tracking across reads); a separate, distinct cause surfaced later (#1322) is terminal emulators with buggy "any-event mouse mode" (ANSI escape 1003) support, such as ConEmu, worked around by avoiding that mode or by `set mouse off`; also distinguished from a different bug where micro fails to reset terminal state on kill/kill -9 leaving stray escape sequences printed after exit, which needed separate terminate-signal handling rather than a tcell fix.

Still open since 2018: current search flow is Ctrl-F, type query, Enter to jump to the first match, then Ctrl-N/Ctrl-P to cycle further matches — pressing Ctrl-N immediately after typing (without Enter) does nothing, which is not discoverable and has confused a steady stream of users for years (several independent "it was Enter all along" rediscoveries through 2026), with the GitHub thread itself becoming the only documentation of the gotcha; zyedidia reportedly ruled out changing the default keybindings, so proposals converged on binding Ctrl-F itself to double as find-first/find-next (a community fork "search-goodies" implemented skip-the-Enter-requirement behavior but was never merged, pending a larger search/replace refactor referenced as #1159); open UX gaps named: Ctrl-N/Ctrl-P don't work to edit/refine the search while the prompt is still open, and there's no live highlighting of all visible matches.

Multiple-cursor support was implemented and merged into master in 2017 (default bindings Alt-N SpawnMultiCursor, Alt-P RemoveMultiCursor, Alt-C RemoveAllMultiCursors, Alt-X SkipMultiCursor, plus Ctrl-click to spawn a cursor at a point), after working through concrete bugs during review: cursors not repositioning when backspace modified the line they depend on (needed cursors to be notified of line edits), extra cursors on the same line double-counting deleted characters, and crashes/duplicate input when two cursors ended up on the same position (fixed by merging coincident cursors) — undo and selection interactions were flagged as still needing more work at merge time. What was NOT implemented, and remained an open gap per later discussion and issue #1255, is Sublime/VSCode's Ctrl-D model: expand cursor-at-word to select the whole word, then each further press adds a cursor at the next matching occurrence (optionally skippable); micro's model is manual placement/removal of cursors rather than incremental word-based multi-select.

Long maintainer back-and-forth (JoeKar/dmaluka) reworking reload, filetype change and autosave: establishes that reload must call SetGlobalOptionNative per changed option rather than re-running InitGlobalSettings, that volatile/local settings must be preserved across reload and filetype change, the split into DoSetOptionNative (no validation/write) vs SetOptionNative (validates and persists), the autosave goroutine redesign to avoid duplicate timers, and known follow-on breakage for plugins that write buf.Settings directly instead of calling SetOptionNative (e.g. detectindent, comment.lua fix included in diff).

Long-running design discussion (JoeKar/dmaluka/Andriamanitra/niten94) on fixing #3794 (long/UTF8 paths breaking backup file names): walks through rejected options (base64, custom escape chars, DEFLATE, a global lookup-table file) before converging on hashing the path only when the URL-encoded name would exceed the 255-char filename limit, writing the original path to a sibling {hash}.path file for recovery, and reusing DetermineEscapePath for both backups and serialized buffers; also fixes a real bug where the hashed fallback name was returned without joining it to the backup dir, which silently wrote backups/serialized buffers into the cwd and caused a gob duplicate-type crash on reopen.

Request-for-help thread that produced the project's actual governance change: zyedidia (sole owner, admittedly stretched thin) named JoeKar and dmaluka as maintainers in March 2024 and gave them PR-merge rights, after community pressure over unreviewed issues/PRs; later comments track moving core dependencies (tcell, json5) into the micro-editor GitHub org while micro itself stays on zyedidia's personal account, and note plugin-channel maintenance being handled separately by taconi. Explains why so many later comments are annotated "maintainer since ~2024".

zyedidia declined to add a built-in Vi/modal editing mode (2016), reasoning that users wanting Vi semantics would be better served by actually using Vim, and that modal support isn't worth the implementation cost relative to other priorities; thread stayed open for years with people pointing at custom Alt-hjkl keybindings as a partial substitute, a 2024 ping toward issue #1740 for true per-mode keybinding sets, and a 2025 proof-of-concept Lua plugin (micro-vi-plugin) attempting modal editing without core changes.

Merged PR fixing FindNext/findUp/findDown so that empty-string patterns like ^, $ and \b only match true line boundaries rather than the edges of the search region when a search starts or ends mid-line; settled on padding the compiled regex with a literal "." on the padded side(s) rather than post-filtering overlapping matches (rejected because regexp.FindAllIndex only returns non-overlapping matches), then extended the same padding/findAll approach into ReplaceRegex so replace -a doesn't suffer the same boundary bug; deliberately deferred unifying findUp/findDown into one function and building a public FindAll/FindAllSubmatch API to separate PRs (#3658, #3552) to keep this fix reviewable.

Open PR implementing tab-bar drag-to-reorder, double-click-to-add and middle-click-to-close, with heavy dmaluka review driving the design: replaces an ad hoc release bool with explicit release/tbClick/tabDrag state on TabList (mirroring Tab.resizing) because relying on a single release flag missed cases like clicking a bufpane then dragging onto the tabbar, or switching tabs mid-press; factors the tab-move logic out of TabMoveCmd into a reusable TabList.MoveTab so both the command and drag gesture share it; and leaves open, as of this packet, how middle-click-to-close should handle tabs containing a mix of modified/unmodified buffers (leaning toward a single all-or-nothing discard prompt) and whether double/middle click conventions should even apply to a terminal-based tab bar.

Merged PR adding $(overwrite) status indicator; key design points: overwrite state is stored on Buffer (not BufPane/Cursor) because Buffer is per-bufpane even when SharedBuffer is shared, same trick as LastSearch/HighlightSearch; [ovwr] and [ro] are mutually exclusive since readonly buffers reject edits anyway (surfaced #1805, readonly overwrite-insert bug, as a separate followup); long bikeshed over indicator text settled on short [ovwr] (not [ins], to avoid wasting statusline space and avoid misleading "insert pressed" reading) placed right after $(modified) in the default statusformatl.

Long-running open issue (2022-2025) about scrolling lag when holding arrow keys; many reporters could not correlate it with CPU/RAM/architecture, but dmaluka (maintainer) confirms it tracks to #2970 (major, CPU-bound) with known contributing bottlenecks #3227 (CPU burned in tcell's CanDisplay(), a terminfo capability check) and #3228 (repeated buf.Settings map lookups); concrete empirical lead from users: setting TERM=vt100 reproduces/worsens the lag while TERM=xterm or xterm-256color removes it, consistent with CanDisplay()'s terminfo-capability-check cost being the hot path on less-capable terminal definitions.

Long-running open PR (since Feb 2025, still active April 2026) reworking Buffer's search/replace API for Lua plugin use: settled design points include renaming the padded-regexp wrapper through RegexpGroup/RegexpSearch to RegexpData (maintainer dmaluka wanted the padding-implementation detail hidden from the public API, not exposed via naming), dropping the useRegex/ignoreCase boolean-flag approach in favor of plain regex strings with inline flags, replacing the internal Loc{-1,-1}/"void" submatch convention with Loc.IsValid(), and processing TextEvent Deltas in reverse order so replaceall does not need to recompute later delta positions; unresolved as of the latest comments is how to support multiline regex matching ($\n$ crossing lines): issue/PR #4068 proposes concatenating all lines into one string, which JoeKar suggested reusing, but tana-gh (the #4068 author) explains that is only a stopgap — without parsing the regex to bound match length under longest-match semantics, correct line-structure-aware matching would need a custom iterator-based regex engine, and whole-string concatenation also breaks ^/$ meaning per-line, so multiline search may need to be a separate API rather than folded into this one.

Merged PR adding matchbracestyle (underline vs highlight, with a match-brace colorscheme field, reverse-video fallback when colorscheme has no match-brace) uncovered and fixed real bugs in brace matching along the way: highlighting the matching brace with reverse colors collided visually with a reverse-video cursor, so highlighting is skipped when the cursor itself sits on the matching brace; deeper issue was FindMatchingBrace's "match brace to the left of cursor" behavior (copied from gedit, which can get away with it because its thin-line cursor reads as between characters, unlike a terminal block cursor) was ambiguous for nested/adjacent braces like ((xyz)) or )( sequences, and the group settled the rule that a brace under the cursor always takes precedence over one to its left, with a minimal one-line fix to FindMatchingBrace's loop-start condition rather than patching the display logic; matchbrace's docs were updated to say "on a brace character or next to it" to reflect the left-of-cursor behavior finally being documented; a residual bug noted but deferred is that nested bracket types (e.g. cursor on `[` in `([xyz])`) highlight both the `[]` and `()` pairs at once.

Merged PR implementing SubWordRight/Left plus Select/Delete variants; maintainer dmaluka ruled that on whitespace SubWord should match the existing WordRight/WordLeft behavior, but on runs of non-word non-whitespace characters (e.g. `foo == bar`) the existing Word behavior is wrong and should skip the run like nano/emacs/gedit do -- and despite masmu arguing mid-thread that touching WordLeft/WordRight was out of scope, the merged diff actually applies that fix to WordRight/WordLeft's cursor.go too; also settled util naming (IsNonAlphaNumeric -> IsNonWordChar, '_' formalized as IsSubwordDelimiter) with "we don't need to add wrappers for everything" as the stated rationale against over-wrapping, and left per-filetype configurable (sub)word delimiters as an unresolved future idea; known residual bug is that trailing whitespace/line-breaks aren't a jump point in either Word or SubWord movement, spun off as #3321.

Terminals typically do not send distinct escape sequences for Backspace vs Ctrl-Backspace, so micro cannot bind them separately in general, but zyedidia pointed out micro already supports the one case where a terminal *does* differentiate (raw pane shows plain Backspace as "Backspace2" and Ctrl-Backspace as "Backspace"): bind Ctrl-Backspace via the key name "OldBackspace" (or "CtrlBackspace"/"CtrlDelete" depending on terminal) to DeleteWordLeft/DeleteWordRight in bindings.json; failing that, Alt-Backspace is bound to DeleteWordLeft by default. This fix was never added to keybindings.md despite repeated requests across years (2021 through 2025), so users keep rediscovering it via this issue instead of the docs.

Tree-sitter syntax highlighting PR (never merged): zyedidia's ruling was not about quality or performance (the author argued perf would match or exceed the existing highlighter, unchallenged) but that the cgo dependency required by go-tree-sitter breaks micro's current cross-compilation setup, so this is out for 2.0 and left open as "could be a good feature for the future" rather than rejected on merits; a separate settled sub-point from the author (p-e-w) is that tree-sitter grammars cannot ship as Lua plugins since grammars are platform-specific compiled binaries, which would need dynamic-linking support in the Lua bridge plus per-platform builds; the author also named an unresolved identity question -- is micro meant to stay nano-like minimal or become a full-featured editor -- and deferred it to zyedidia, who never answered it in-thread; a 2024 revival floated compiling grammars to WASM and running them via the pure-Go wazero runtime to sidestep cgo entirely, with a performance caveat raised but never tested; sibling proposal is #1453 (TextMate grammar files).

Long-running issue on emacs/vim-style multi-key sequences (e.g. Ctrl-x Ctrl-f): zyedidia initially called a vim-keybindings plugin not worth the effort ("I don't really see too much reason for a vim user to use micro over vim"), but reversed in 2020 once PR #1299 added multi-key sequence support to the binding system, calling upgrading the keybinding system to support key sequences "the highest priority feature at the moment" so that vim or emacs bindings could then be implemented as a plugin on top of it; nano-style remapping (CtrlO->Save, CtrlK->CutLine etc. via bindings.json) and Lua-side BindKey() in init.lua were both already possible without this work. As of 2025 a third-party vi-mode Lua plugin (akikareha/micro-vi-plugin) exists built on the onBeforeTextEvent hook, still early-stage, rather than anything landed in core.

Long-running Windows Terminal paste bug (stair-step/cascading indentation on multi-line paste) finally diagnosed: Windows Terminal (unlike conhost) doesn't request ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, so it swallows Ctrl-v/Ctrl-Shift-v/Shift-Ins itself and forwards the clipboard content to micro as individual keystrokes rather than as a bracketed-paste (EventPaste) sequence, so micro's autoindent logic (which the "edit" editor explicitly skips via a `raw` flag on true paste) fires per inserted line and staircases the indentation; root fix requires tcell to properly negotiate ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT and parse bracketed paste on Windows, which JoeKar confirmed works on the in-progress tcell/v3 branch (with a known residual redraw bug when pasting over a selection). Workarounds documented in-thread: rebind Paste to a non-intercepted key like Alt-v, or wrap Ctrl-v as "command:setlocal autoindent off,Paste,command:setlocal autoindent on" in bindings.json; setting clipboard to external/terminal and the paste on/off toggle are also discussed but are each only a partial fix depending on terminal.

Merged PR adding C/C++ digit-separator (0b0000'0000, 0x0AB0'aA20) support exposed a structural bug in micro's region-based regex highlighter: a quoted-region's "skip" pattern cannot reliably prevent the region from leaking highlighting across to a later same-delimiter token on the same line (e.g. a char literal right after a separator-containing number), which dmaluka says is actually fixed by the separate highlighter rewrite in #3127 ("significantly improve performance") rather than fixable by better regex alone, so this PR ships an "[[:graph:]]{2,}'" error-regex workaround with a TODO to revert once #3127 lands; dmaluka also measured the added regexes' cost directly -- initial highlighting of a ~40000-line C file went from ~800ms to ~1s -- and argued against porting the complex rules to c.yaml on a benefit/cost basis (C23 digit separators are rarely used) versus Neko-Box-Coder's consistency argument, settled by checking cpp.yaml's own filetype-detection signature so .h headers aren't misclassified as C in the first place; a regression surfaced 16 months after merge (enum value names now wrongly highlighted as constant.number), spawning follow-up fixes #3870/#3891/#3905.

Merged fix for a sudo-write race: the old sucmd-dd-based safe-write started one "notrunc" dd process early in openFile() and a second untruncated dd later, which under sudo-rs's stricter auditable-escalation enforcement raced on TCGETS2/TCSETS2 ioctls for the password prompt and, on failure, left the TTY corrupted because tcell's TempStart()/Init() just re-snapshots whatever (possibly corrupted) terminal state is current rather than restoring a known-good one; dmaluka traced the original notrunc split back to PR #3807's discussion -- it existed specifically so a failed sudo invocation (e.g. wrong password) wouldn't truncate the real file before the backup was made -- so the fix had to preserve that safety: drop notrunc (dd truncates naturally on open, leaving only one sudo process so the race can't happen) and reorder safeWrite() so that, in the sudo path only, writeBackup() runs before openFile() and a failed openFile() returns util.OverwriteError pointing at the already-created backup; non-sudo path keeps backup-after-open since open there is non-destructive. Known accepted regression: if sudo fails to even start (e.g. binary missing), this still creates a now-unneeded backup, mitigated by an exec.LookPath(sucmd) pre-check but not eliminated for other sudo-start failures. Separately flagged but deliberately left for tcell itself: micro's custom pristine-terminal-state capture/restore duplicates logic tcell already has (and upstream tcell's Suspend()/Resume() would be the right primitive if backported/fixed), so this PR's screen.go capture/restore is a stopgap, not the final design.

Merged PR adding a truecolor option (auto/on/off); maintainers established that tcell already autodetects truecolor via COLORTERM and micro only needs to set TCELL_TRUECOLOR=enable/disable, with MICRO_TRUECOLOR=1 kept as a backward-compatible override of auto, defaulting to auto.

PR added +/-/~ prefixes to the goto command for relative line jumps, but this broke the pre-existing nano-style convention where a bare negative number jumped inward from the end of the file (#1691); it was merged, then reverted months later after a user regression report, with maintainers agreeing the underlying question (vim-style relative vs nano-style negative-from-end, possibly as separate commands) needs re-litigating in #2897 rather than being settled here.

Docs-only PR clarifying plugin callback semantics: postinit() runs after init() has run for all plugins (not just the plugin's own init), a new deinit() cleanup callback runs on unload/reload, and the reload command unloads every plugin via deinit() then reinitializes via preinit/init/postinit; also settled that plugin docs rendered in-editor as plain text must stay readable without markdown rendering, so Go-doc links get moved to trailing "Relevant links" blocks rather than inlined into signatures.

Merged PR adding independent CursorToViewTop/Center/Bottom actions (bind directly to keys, not meant for chaining with PageUp/PageDown), with review establishing the correct soft-wrap-aware way to test whether the cursor is within the current view (compare SLoc via h.SLocFromLoc against v.StartLine/view height, not raw line numbers); discussion also surfaced the longstanding separate question (#1808) of whether CursorPageUp/CursorPageDown should instead be changed to nano-style behavior that preserves the cursor's relative position in the view across page moves, which the PR author said would be addressed as new actions in a follow-up PR rather than here.

Merged PR removed the canMatchStart/canMatchEnd optimization in pkg/highlight/highlighter.go (which skipped re-matching ^/$ anchored regexes per fragment) because it incorrectly conflated per-line regex anchors with true text start/end, causing many syntax-highlighting bugs across sh/php/js/c/vi rules (13 issues referenced); zyedidia acknowledged this may cost some incremental-highlighting performance but accepted the tradeoff, noting the real fix is the stalled from-scratch highlighter rework (flare) that mostly just needs language files now.

Merged bug fix for ReloadSettings(true) not firing onBufferOptionChanged/OptionCallback when filetype changed on reload; review split the old InitLocalSettings into UpdatePathGlobLocals (glob-matched local settings, must use absolute path or cd-relative opens silently fail to match) and UpdateFileTypeLocals (ft: local settings, applied after UpdateRules once the filetype is known), with a caught regression where glob locals briefly stopped applying until the next reload, and a deliberate decision to ignore a filetype key inside an ft: block to avoid unpredictable recursive overrides.

Merged PR making open/term commands skip the save prompt for shared buffers (mirroring Quit/#3559) by factoring the prompt into a shared closePrompt helper; review surfaced a broader unresolved inconsistency, still unfixed here, in when plugin action callbacks fire: onSave fires for the open/term/quit close-prompt saves and for `save` with no args but onSaveAs fires for `save <path>`, preSave only fires when the key-bound Save action itself is pressed (not from these prompts), and the onAction docs wrongly imply callbacks only fire from direct key-bound triggering; dmaluka concluded documentation should be improved to match reality but that fully unifying the behavior is probably not worth doing.

Merged PR reworking plugin_installer.go error reporting for unreachable/malformed plugin repos: settled on using http.StatusText(resp.StatusCode) rather than per-status-code custom messages (dmaluka's suggestion), and on returning nil instead of PluginPackages{} from Fetch functions for consistency across the error paths; final format is "Skipped: <url>" followed by a " Reason: ..." line.

Merged PR adding a (built-in) marker to `-plugin list` output and renaming the Plugin.Default field to Builtin for clarity; settled that built-in plugins show "(built-in)" instead of a version number (since their version is never bumped), that init.lua is a special case shown bare (neither built-in nor versioned, but still listed so users know it exists), and that removal of a built-in plugin now names which plugin was blocked rather than a generic "Default plugins cannot be removed" message.

Merged PR fixing proportional HSplit/VSplit resize breaking after quitting a pane inside nested splits, caused by "chained parent" nodes (a parent with exactly one child) left behind in the split tree; fix adds a flatten() that removes chained parents and also collapses a successor node whose Kind matches its new parent's Kind, calling markSizes() afterward so propW/propH stay consistent with new siblings. Review surfaced that propScale/propW/propH-based proportional resize is already unreliable more broadly (related issue #3071, later crash issue #3980), so this PR narrows but does not fully close that gap.

Merged doc-only PR (man page + micro -help) clarifying the FILE:LINE:COL and +LINE:COL cursor-position syntax, settling several previously-undocumented semantics: FILE[:LINE[:COL]] only works when the parsecursor option is enabled and applies per-file; +LINE[:COL] always works regardless of parsecursor but applies only to the last such flag and then to every FILE argument given (even an unnamed empty buffer, so "micro +10:20" does not try to open a file literally named +10:20); the two forms are mutually exclusive and +LINE:COL takes priority when both are present (e.g. "micro foo:10 bar +20" opens both foo and bar at line 20, ignoring foo's :10).

Merged PR fixing a long-standing data race between the async syntax highlighter and main-goroutine buffer edits (surfaced by PRs #3062/#3208 enabling InitRuntimeFiles in tests, investigated in #3220): replaces the old per-line rehighlight-only locking with a single whole-LineArray lock (Lock/Unlock) that callers like the highlighter take explicitly around each line access, settling on explicit caller-managed locking over a larger lock-everything API because only the highlighter and a few direct-data-mutation call sites (insert/remove, and Buffer.Retab which bypasses the EventHandler) actually touch shared state concurrently; LinesNum() must be checked after acquiring the lock in the same iteration rather than cached up front, since the line count can shrink between check and access. Follow-on race-adjacent work: #3237 (ReHighlightStates startline sanity-check), #3291 (diffgutter race fix).

Closed issue: Shift/Ctrl+Arrow keyboard selection (not mouse) didn't work over PuTTY. Maintainer root-caused it as a PuTTY-side bug, not fixable in micro/tcell: older PuTTY sends the wrong escape codes for shift/ctrl+arrow; KiTTY (a PuTTY fork) was found to send correct codes. A 2024 follow-up comment gives the actual fix for modern PuTTY: Terminal -> Keyboard -> "Shift/Ctrl/Alt with the arrow keys" set to "xterm-style bitmap" (confirmed on PuTTY 0.79).

Closed issue requesting a transparent/terminal-matching background, resolved entirely in comments rather than code: any 16-color colorscheme (list in runtime/help/colors.md#16-color, e.g. the built-in "simple" scheme via `set colorscheme simple`) lets the terminal's own background show through, because 16-color schemes omit an explicit background; alternatively a custom colorscheme can omit `color-link default "[fg],[bg]"` entirely, or set the bg to an alpha-zero hex value like `#00000000`, to force transparency explicitly.

Merged PR adding util.ResolvePath() (absolute path + filepath.EvalSymlinks) and storing it as Buffer.AbsPath, so opening the same file through different symlinks/relative paths shares one SharedBuffer (fixes #3995). Settled design points from a long review: must resolve symlinks component-by-component including non-existent trailing path segments (EvalSymlinks errors on a not-yet-existing file, so ResolvePath walks back to the nearest existing ancestor, resolves that, then rejoins the remainder); the absolute path itself must be resolved too, since the CWD can itself contain symlinks, not just the given relative path; serialization of cursor/undo state on buffer close was narrowed to only happen for the last (non-shared) instance of a buffer, since earlier closes were pointlessly overwriting it; and the displayed file name/statusline path is left as "whichever path was used to open the file first" (matching vim's actual, if non-obvious, behavior) while AbsPath alone is the resolved identity used for comparison. Related follow-up crash: #4131 (QuitAll).

Merged PR reworking the sh.yaml "conditional flags" statement regex that highlights CLI options, after a long back-and-forth on edge cases: settled on `(\s|^)(--?[A-Za-z0-9][\w-]*)` to match hyphenated single- and double-dash options including numbers/underscores/capitals and combined value forms like `-Dval,with,commas` or `--opt=value`; deliberately chose not to special-case single-letter double-dash options like `--a` or GNU's truncated-long-option style (e.g. `cat --v` for `--version`) since "we shouldn't try to be too smart" and highlighting that pops on/off character-by-character is more confusing than occasionally mis-highlighting a bare `---------` run; a leading/trailing `\s` is still consumed by the match (so with a background-colored theme a visible space gets highlighted too), accepted as a known imperfection given Go regexp has no lookahead/lookbehind. Related follow-up: #3894 (multi-word flags).

PR reworks the comment plugin to support multi-cursor comment/uncomment: gather every cursor's selected lines into one shared set, toggle the comment state once for the union, then restore each cursor by a computed X displacement (comment-marker length, signed by whether lines were commented or uncommented); review caught a real bug where the shared lines table got clobbered between cursors, and the fix adds an exception so a selection ending in a trailing newline no longer comments the blank line after it, preserving prior single-cursor behavior.

Root cause of the "ctrl-v pastes stale cut text instead of what was ctrl-c'd" reports: with clipboard set to internal (the default in some setups), micro never touches the system clipboard at all, so ctrl-v only has access to whatever micro itself last cut/copied internally, while the terminal/OS intercepts ctrl-c/ctrl-v against the system clipboard; fix is to set clipboard to external so micro reads/writes the OS clipboard directly. On WSL this is harder since there's no xclip/X server, workaround is a fake xclip/xsel shim backed by clip.exe (e.g. Konfekt/xclip-xsel-WSL) placed early on PATH.

Fixes a crash when a chained-action keybinding (e.g. mapping that opens a terminal mid-chain) switches the current pane away from a BufPane: BufMapEvent/bufAction now breaks the chain once MainTab().CurPane() returns nil instead of continuing to dereference it, fixing #2288/#2307; maintainers kept the Lua-exported CurPane() typed as *action.BufPane (not the generic Pane interface) because gopher-luar gives Lua plugins no way to type-assert/downcast a polymorphic return, so a plugin needs CurPane() to fail fast rather than silently alias a TermPane/InfoPane/RawPane as a BufPane — this still leaves chained actions and onAction/preAction callbacks unsupported for non-buf panes, it only stops them from crashing. Side discussion also exposed that bufAction's success/innerSuccess return value is effectively unused/confusing dead logic, deliberately left alone here and addressed separately in PR #3267.

Adds hltaberrors (highlight tabs where tabstospaces expects spaces, or leading spaces where it expects tabs) and hltrailingws (highlight trailing whitespace) options, both off by default; hltrailingws is deliberately "smart" — a cursor's own newly-typed trailing whitespace on the active line is tracked via NewTrailingWsY and left unhighlighted until the cursor moves off that line, so normal typing doesn't flash red, which is tracked through undo/redo and cursor-shift-from-line-insert-or-remove to survive those operations; maintainer dmaluka deliberately kept this orthogonal to auto-indent (auto-indent still copies a line's existing indentation even if that indentation is flagged as an error) reasoning that coupling them to "fix" the error on new lines would create partially-mixed indentation inside a block rather than solve the real mess. The PR also surfaces a multi-year maintainer-responsiveness complaint that spawned a governance discussion (#3161) about decentralizing admin/merge rights beyond the single owner.

Micro has no built-in delete-line-without-clipboard action — Ctrl-K is cut (SelectLine+Cut) and overwrites the clipboard/system buffer, which is a real nuisance over SSH with X11 forwarding since cut/copy triggers a noticeable clipboard-sync delay; the documented workaround is rebinding to a composed action, e.g. {"CtrlK": "SelectLine,Delete"}, which deletes the line in place without touching the clipboard, though the Alt-g on-screen bindings help list is static and keeps showing the default "^K Cut line" label even after such a rebind.

Adds vim-style `+/REGEX` CLI argument (e.g. `micro +/imem_size +623 file.c`) alongside the existing `+LINE[:COL]`, with argument order determining whether the search moves the cursor after the line/col jump (SearchAfterStart); implemented by replacing NewBufferFromFileAtLoc/NewBufferFromStringAtLoc's bare cursorLoc parameter with a buffer.Command struct {StartCursor, SearchRegex, SearchAfterStart} threaded through NewBuffer, which runs FindNext and sets LastSearch/HighlightSearch if a match is found at buffer-open time; review flagged a latent crash-safety concern (regexp.MustCompile on would-be user-controlled patterns, as previously caused the #3700 crash on `+/\Q`) but concluded this PR only MustCompiles its own constant arg-parsing regexes, while the user-supplied search text goes through the same FindNext path ordinary interactive search already uses — meaning the known FindNext regex-crash class (#3700) is a pre-existing architectural gap, not something this PR introduces or fixes.

Fixes the #3700 crash where a search/replace regex containing an unterminated \Q (quote-literal start without a closing \E) blew up: findLineParams pads the user regex with a wrapping non-capturing group plus boundary dots (e.g. ".(?:"+r.String()+")") when checking word boundaries, and that wrapping used regexp.MustCompile, which panics if the padded string is invalid — and an unterminated \Q, while valid Go regexp syntax on its own (confirmed upstream via golang/go#76424), becomes invalid once more text is appended after it. Fix detects this case by trying to compile r.String()+"\\E" first; if that succeeds, it's used as the base before padding, so the \Q is implicitly closed; the check only runs when padMode is nonzero (padStart/padEnd), avoiding a needless extra compile on every line. Because both interactive search and the `replace`/`replaceall` command path go through this same findLineParams, fixing it here protects both — before this PR, \Q without \E crashed FindNext-based search but was silently "accepted" (and correctly applied) by ReplaceRegex, a related but distinct crash path reported separately.

Maintainer zyedidia declined to change micro's default indentation from tabs to spaces, reasoning that the tab key inserting a literal tab character is the sane baseline and that per-user preference belongs in the existing `tabstospaces` setting rather than being flipped as a global default (citing Go's own tab convention as added context, not the core reason); micro has no built-in per-file indentation auto-detection, the documented workaround is the third-party plugin micro-detectindent (dmaluka/micro-detectindent) combined with `tabstospaces`.

For copy/paste over SSH, there's a third clipboard mode beyond internal/external: "clipboard": "terminal", which uses the OSC 52 terminal escape sequence so the remote micro process asks the local terminal emulator to set its clipboard directly, with no X11 round trip — works with terminals that implement OSC 52 (e.g. Alacritty) and gives working Ctrl-C/Ctrl-V with no added latency. The xclip/xsel + `ssh -X` approach (X11 forwarding so micro's external-clipboard calls reach the local X server) also works but is reported consistently slow (roughly 0.5-2+ seconds per copy/paste, some report 15s for mouse selection) because every selection round-trips through the X11 tunnel; in terminals without OSC 52 support, the fallback is to let Ctrl+Shift+C/Ctrl+Shift+V (terminal-native clipboard ownership, independent of micro's own Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V) do the copy/paste instead, holding Shift while mouse-selecting so the terminal grabs the selection rather than micro.

Flathub distribution was added by a community contributor (blt-r) rather than the maintainer: after owner zyedidia approved publishing, several follow-up PRs were needed to fix metainfo.xml/appdata issues (invisible characters, missing fields) before the app would even show up as an "application" in the Flathub store (needed type="desktop-application" in the appdata component) — flathub.org/apps/details/io.github.zyedidia.micro. Flatpak installs are sandboxed: config lives under ~/.var/app/io.github.zyedidia.micro/config/micro instead of the usual ~/.config/micro, and flatpak packages cannot install an executable onto PATH, so running it as plain `micro` requires a user-created shell alias/function wrapping `flatpak run io.github.zyedidia.micro`; as of the last comment the Flathub listing was still unverified (no response on requesting Flathub's app-author verification).

Fixes a crash (#3980) in the split tree's Node logic: root-node detection had relied on Kind==STUndef, but once the first VSplit/HSplit set the root's Kind to STVert/STHoriz that marker became permanently wrong, breaking Unsplit's special-casing of the root; fix switches the check to n.parent==nil (the actual definition of "is root"), used consistently in VSplit/HSplit/flatten. Fixing this naively caused two further crashes the reviewer found by hand (unsplitting the leftmost pane of a fresh VSplit; closing all panes in a 4-way split starting from a nested branch) — flatten()'s root-node special case must copy the single remaining child's children back onto the root in place (*n = *n.children[0]; reparent children to n) rather than just marking it undef, and Kind must only be forced back to STUndef when the flattened root ends up with zero children, since a root that inherits multiple grandchildren still needs a real STVert/STHoriz for proportional resize to work. Settled design: STUndef is kept (not removed) specifically to avoid passing a meaningless STVert/STHoriz into NewNode() for a just-created single-pane root, and the tree's debug String() only prints the root as a bare node with no "-"/"|" marker when it truly has no children/orientation.

Owner zyedidia gives a detailed account of modifier-key escape sequences across terminals: the xterm pc-style code convention (2=Shift,3=Alt,4=Shift+Alt,5=Ctrl,6=Shift+Ctrl,7=Alt+Ctrl,8=all three), concrete iTerm2 vs Alacritty escape dumps for Ctrl/Alt/Shift+Arrows, and the rule that Alt+char is just ESC+char (e.g. Alt-n = \x1bn) while Alt+Arrow needs \x1b[1;3A/B/C/D; also notes Alacritty sends unicode chars for Alt on macOS instead of escape sequences and lacks an escape-prefix option like iTerm2's "Esc+" setting.
